comparison: tirzepatide vs subcutaneous semaglutide (weight loss, obesity)

Risk of bias.note: Not auto-rated. Most trials industry-sponsored; some open-label. Panel must complete RoB-2.

Inconsistency.note: I^2(semaglutide 2.4mg, dose-matched) = 93.9% -> high, BUT largely explained by follow-up (44-104 wk) and population; panel may judge as explained (not downgrade). Star network -> incoherence NOT assessable.

Indirectness.note: Applicability to the real-world obese target population is MEASURED, not judged: effects transported (tirz 17.5, sema 14.6 pp), ranking survives (POTH 0.898). NB: a CV-benefit claim WOULD be downgraded for indirectness -- weight loss is not a validated CV surrogate (extend_surrogate.json, I^2_HR=0%).

Imprecision.note: Contrast 2.9 pp, 95% CrI [-0.17, 5.97] crosses null AND the MID (2 pp) -> SERIOUS. (CrI is CONSERVATIVE -- independent marginals; exact NMA contrast is narrower, needs joint posterior.)

Publication / reporting bias.note: MEASURED not inferred: 6 posted-but-unpublished ghosts identified (AACTxPubMed); the observed pull is negligible (-0.12 pp) and Egger asymmetry was shown to be heterogeneity, not suppression.

etd.judgement: Obesity pharmacotherapy selection between two incretins
tirzepatide ~+2.9 pp more weight loss; both on the benefit-risk frontier (true)
tirzepatide more nausea (22% vs 16%); ~2.19 pp nausea per extra pp weight loss
PANEL INPUT: patients weight maximal loss vs GI tolerability differently
PANEL INPUT: relative price, access, administration

draft_recommendation: CONDITIONAL (weak) recommendation: tirzepatide MAY be preferred where greater weight loss is prioritised, but the additional benefit is uncertain (low certainty); choice should weigh tolerability and cost
guardrails: no CV-benefit claim from weight (not a validated surrogate)
every rating traceable + re-runnable from cited data
